# Agatha Sowerby

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c9 P16](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0016)</sub>
- **Role:** Dressmaker and domestic artisan  <sub>[v2 c8 P0](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0000)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Agatha  <sub>[v2 c8 P0](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0000), [v2 c19 P62](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0062)</sub>; Mrs. Agatha  <sub>[v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v2 c8 P0](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0000), [v2 c25 P70](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0070)</sub>; Mrs. Agatha Sowerby  <sub>[v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v2 c8 P0](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0000), [v4 c10 P60](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0060)</sub>

## Appearance

She is described as a heavy woman.

_Sources: [v1 c9 P19](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0019)_

## Personality

Mrs. Sowerby is candid, outspoken, and prides herself on voicing her opinions without fear or partiality. Though seen by some neighbors as an inveterate meddler and gossip, she possesses a compassionate heart, regularly aids the needy, and shows warmth and hospitality to new neighbors. She is deeply practical and religious, holding strong opinions on proper behavior and domestic duties.

_Sources: [v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000), [v2 c9 P3](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0003), [v2 c9 P10](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0010), [v2 c25 P61](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0061), [v2 c25 P70](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0070)_

## History

Mrs. Agatha Sowerby resides in Sowerby's Hollow near Brierley with her husband, Thomas. She watched Obed Abernethy bring the orphan Nell into the neighborhood and later observed Thirza Abernethy taking in the twins, Robin and Lucy Farrow. When meeting young Nell at Thirza's home, Mrs. Sowerby bluntly criticized the girl's thin frame, freckles, and red hair, provoking a passionate outburst from Nell. Despite Mr. Pettifer's complaints about her persistent fundraising for a vestry room carpet and her blunt style of speaking, Nell came to appreciate Mrs. Sowerby's underlying generosity, such as her forgiveness when Timothy Cotton took butter from her dairy. As her husband Thomas's health fluctuated, she spent much of her time caring for him, though she took advantage of his periods of improvement to take trips into town, visit neighbors like the newly returned Mrs. Pettifer, and continue participating in local community life.

_Sources: [v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v1 c9 P15](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0015), [v1 c9 P16](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0016), [v1 c9 P27](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0027), [v1 c9 P30](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0030), [v2 c8 P0](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0000), [v2 c8 P1](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0001), [v2 c8 P2](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0002), [v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000), [v2 c9 P2](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0002), [v2 c9 P10](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0010), [v2 c19 P62](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0062), [v2 c25 P61](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0061), [v2 c25 P67](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0067), [v2 c25 P70](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0070)_
